sections.h2: Which government bills a Cary home for property tax?
sections.html:
The county does, not the town. Town limits now reach into Wake, Chatham and Durham counties. Whichever county holds the parcel values it, bills it and collects the town's tax along with its own.

Your parcel's location decides which county applies, and your bill or the county's online search will tell you. These are the numbers to use:

  • Wake County Tax Administration, 919-856-5400. Walk-in help is at 301 S. McDowell St., Suite 3800, Raleigh, weekdays 8:30 to 5:00.
  • Chatham County Collection Division, 919-542-8250.
  • Durham County Tax Administrator, 919-560-0300.

Under a local agreement Wake mails the bills and takes in payment for every town and special district within the county. A Cary owner in Wake pays one bill with the county and town rates together. Questions about how the town rate was set go to the town. The town also adds a $30 vehicle license fee that rides on the vehicle tax bill, with no sticker.

sections.h2: Cary and Wake County tax rates
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2027 the town rate is 36.75 cents per $100 and the Wake County rate is 53.71 cents per $100. A bill adds the two when the parcel is in Wake.

The Cary Town Council adopted its budget raising the town rate by 2.75 cents. The budget also sets a solid waste and recycling fee of $28 per month. That is billed on its own and is not part of the property tax rate. Wake's commissioners raised the county rate by 2 cents to reach 53.71 cents.

The rates are multiplied by assessed value, which makes that value as important as either rate. After a revaluation the rate can move in either direction. Chatham and Durham County parcels carry those counties' own rates, which you can get from the numbers above. Rates reset every July 1 with the budgets, so rely on the current bill instead of last year's figure.

Taxes are due September 1. Anything paid by January 5 carries no extra charge. Interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

You can pay Wake in pieces of any size with no approval needed, so long as the balance is cleared by January 5. A statement showing what remains follows each payment. If your lender pays through escrow, no paper bill is mailed to you, and the online lookup shows the amount. Wake takes ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and the four major credit cards.

sections.h2: How revaluation affects a Cary home's value
sections.html:
Wake's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2024. The next is effective January 1, 2027, and a two-year cycle follows. State law requires a reappraisal only every eighth year, so Wake revalues far more often than the minimum.

Wake works through neighborhooding, sales-based pricing of land and buildings, field and office review, and finally the notice of assessment with its appeal review. The county sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods, and its commissioners approve the resulting Schedule of Values. The 2027 schedule has results before the Board on January 19, 2027, value notices out by January 22, 2027, and an appeal deadline planned for April 30, 2027.

If you dispute the notice, take the case to the county's review board. A loss at the board leads to the Property Tax Commission. Notice must be filed within 30 days of the mailed decision, as G.S. 105-290 sets out. Wake runs a call center for questions on the 2027 round at 919-857-3800.

Wake County runs three state programs for Cary owners in its portion: the Senior and Disabled Program, Tax Deferment and the Disabled Veteran Program. The programs cover low-income owners 65 and older, low-income owners who are 100% disabled, and those with a total, permanent service-connected disability, along with unmarried surviving spouses.

  • Age or disability: the 2026 income limit is $38,800, and a qualifying home loses whichever is more, $25,000 or half its appraised value, from the taxable amount.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of appraised value comes off, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years of owning and living in the home, the bill is limited to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% where income is above $38,800 and at most $58,200.

State law sets June 1. Wake looks at late applications one by one, for good cause, through December 31 of the same year. Forgetting or not knowing about a program is typically not good cause. Wake's examples that do count are illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment and a delay in getting disability certification. An owner gets one program, not a stack, so ask the tax office which one fits. G.S. 105-277.1 has the exclusion rules.

sections.h2: What if I cannot pay my Cary property tax?
sections.html:
Call Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 before January 6. Wake can set up short-term payment plans, earlier calls leave more options, and it cannot help once a bill becomes overdue.

State law permits past due taxes to be taken from paychecks, bank accounts or rent. The parcel lien arises under G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 finishes with an auction at the courthouse door, though redemption remains possible before confirmation.

If a Cary house also has a mortgage in default, the tax lien and the lender's foreclosure can run at the same time, which narrows the timeline. If you sell before an auction, the price stays with you, minus the tax paid at closing.

Cary had an estimated 183,582 people in July 2025. Owned homes had a median value of $580,200 across 2020-2024, and two in three units, 66.6%, are lived in by their owners.

Sequence matters. First work out which county holds the parcel, then call it for the balance on every bill, find out whether a relief claim or deferral is on file, and hand the written figures to the closing attorney. If taxes are behind, the county's short-term payment plan is worth a call before listing, since options shrink once a bill is overdue.

Check your value notice after each revaluation, since assessed value is half of the tax calculation. At listing time, get a payoff figure from whichever county holds your parcel. The closing attorney then pays that year's open tax from what you receive. Recording happens at that same county's register of deeds. Wake's register sets the excise tax at $2 per thousand dollars of price. With a cash buyer there is no lender escrow to unwind, and the tax is simply settled at the table.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay Cary property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay the county that holds your parcel: Wake, Chatham or Durham. Wake, Chatham and Durham each assess, bill and collect for the parcels inside their own borders, town tax included.

faqs.q: What is the Cary town property tax rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2027 the town charges 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, a 2.75 cent increase. Wake County's rate is 53.71 cents per $100, and Wake collects both for parcels in its portion.

faqs.q: When does Wake County interest begin on Cary taxes?
faqs.a: It begins January 6, so paying by January 5 avoids it. The charge is 2% to February 1, then three-fourths of a percent monthly.

faqs.q: When is the next Wake County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027, with a two-year rhythm after that. Wake plans to send value notices by January 22, 2027.

faqs.q: Can a Cary senior reduce a property tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly, if age or disability and income tests are met. The exclusion removes $25,000 or half the value, whichever is bigger. File by June 1, though late filings can be weighed for good cause.
